blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, which of these may a subtype do to the contract of its base type?

options.text: Accept a wider range of inputs than its base type accepts
options.says: The page says a subtype can weaken preconditions, accepting more inputs.

options.text: Refuse some of the inputs that its base type does accept
options.says: The page says preconditions cannot be strengthened: a subtype cannot reject what the base accepts.

options.text: Promise less about its results than its base type does
options.says: The page says postconditions cannot be weakened: a subtype must deliver at least what the base promises.

questions.stem: Per this page, why does the Java community generally accept Collections.unmodifiableList() although its add() throws?

options.text: Its add() is documented by List as an optional operation
options.says: The page says List.add() is documented as optional and may throw UnsupportedOperationException.

options.text: Its add() is declared by a read-only interface, not by List
options.says: The page says it implements List and throws on mutation; its static type is still List.

options.text: Its add() is rejected by the compiler rather than at run time
options.says: The page shows unmodifiable.add("d") compiling and throwing UnsupportedOperationException when it runs.

concepts: Collections.unmodifiableList() throwing on add() is accepted because List documents add() as an optional operation.
A subtype may weaken a precondition or strengthen a postcondition, and never the reverse.
